name: Semnam
confidence_why: 3 independent first-hand sources agree (2 agree, 0 refine), none contradicts

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-dominant, final stress' rests on the only existing description of Semnam, a 2009 first-hand phonology sketch by the primary fieldworker; the deciding sentence is verified verbatim in the now-downloaded PDF (correct the locator from p. 285 to p. 284), and the same paper's ~670 stress-marked phonetic transcriptions are uniformly final-stressed, with Matisoff 2003 confirming the Aslian-wide final (major-syllable) stress pattern. No grammar, later phonology or instrumental study of Semnam/Lanoh exists (Glottolog: 0 descriptive refs; web search nil), so no better source can change the classification. Action: record the copy we hold, fix the page locator, fill the empty grade field citing p. 284 + §3.5 p. 292 transcriptions; no reclassification.

sources.citation: Burenhult & Wegener 2009, JSEALS 1:283-312, full PDF re-read via Internet Archive copy of jseals.org/p. 285)
sources.quote: As in other Aslian languages, the full range of phonemes is only to be found in the last, stressed syllable of words.

sources.citation: Burenhult, Niclas & Claudia Wegener. 2009. Preliminary notes on the phonology, orthography and vocabulary of Semnam (Austroasiatic, Malay Peninsula). Journal of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society 1: 283-312.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'As in other Aslian languages, the full range of phonemes is only to be found in the last, stressed syllable of words.' (p. 284); all ~670 stress-marked phonetic forms in the glossary show final stress, e.g. [pək˺ˈpaːk˺], [kələŋˈkɛːgŋ], [biˈjɘːᵈn].
sources.locator: p. 284 (PDF p. 290); also p. 290, p. 292 §3.5, appendix glossary pp. 295-312

sources.citation: Matisoff, James A. 2003. Aslian: Mon-Khmer of the Malay Peninsula. Mon-Khmer Studies 33: 1-58.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: Family-level only: Aslian sesquisyllables consist of a 'major' syllable with fully-stressed vowel preceded by a 'minor' syllable; in true disyllables the non-final vowel is unstressed. Semnam appears only in the language abbreviation list, no Semnam-specific stress statement.
sources.note: Family-level Aslian overview stating major (final) syllable carries stress; corroborates the 'as in other Aslian languages' premise of our deciding quote. downloaded now; confirms.

sources.citation: Phillips, Timothy C. 2012. Proto-Aslian: towards an understanding of its historical linguistic systems, principles and processes. PhD thesis, Institut Alam dan Tamadun Melayu, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia.
